Partly, it may be a desire __to stop__ emotions in front of strangers.
solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Quell"** means to put an end to something, typically by the use of force; to suppress or subdue. (दबाना)

 
 
• **Example: **The police were called in to** quell** the riot.
 
 
 
• **"Stop"** refers to bringing something to an end or halting its progress. (रोकना)
 
 
• **Example: **She tried to** stop** the bleeding with a piece of cloth.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that "quell" is used to express the meaning of "stop" in a context of suppression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Smash** (तोड़ना): To break something into pieces violently.

 
 
• **Example:** He **smashed** the vase in a fit of anger.
 
 
 
• **Quiet** (शांत): To make or become silent or calm.
 
 
• **Example:** She asked the children to **quiet** down.
 
 
 
• **Put out** (बुझाना): To extinguish something, such as a fire.
 
 
• **Example:** The firefighters managed to **put out **the blaze quickly.
